nodes.label: Badge refresh mechanism (diff, lock, store)
nodes.rationale: refresh() recomputes earned() and diffs it against the stored Badge rows rather than maintaining incremental state, under the one-row BadgeRefresh lock so a cron run and an admin action serialize. It deletes computed rows no longer earned (keeping an inactive duplicate first so a revocation survives, else the lowest id), bulk_creates the new ones, and leaves the rest untouched so created_at and a revoked row's is_active survive across runs. nodes.label: Local-id to production-id mapping via save_base(raw=True)
nodes.rationale: A plain dumpdata/loaddata cannot be used: auto-increment ids differ between the two databases, loaddata upserts by id and would silently overwrite production rows, and auth.User is shared across editions so returning players already exist on production under different ids. The importer therefore maps every local `_id` to a fresh production id through a per-table dict and never writes `_id` to the database, and inserts every row with Model.save_base(raw=True) (the same call loaddata uses) so overridden save() methods — which schedule games, create team results, re-parse the registration CSV, apply score deltas — never run on import.

nodes.label: Game.is_played manual flag
nodes.rationale: A game previously had no status: scores defaulted to 0-0 and organisers deliberately mixed rounds so players could rest, so round.is_over could not say whether a given game was actually played. Game.is_played is added as a manual boolean, editable in the admin changelist, so the schedule UI and the reveal rule can distinguish a scheduled pairing from a played result. Game.save() still grants the 0-0 draw point to both teams on creation, so unplayed games already sit inside the ranking's league points; reconciling that was left as accepted debt for the follow-up points-from-played-games spec.

nodes.label: League points recomputed from played games, not deltas
nodes.rationale: Game.save() previously applied score deltas to TeamResult.points, granting a draw point on creation for every scheduled 0-0 game and permanently desyncing points if a score were edited outside save(). The new rule recomputes a team's league points from scratch — 3 per win, 1 per draw, 0 per loss — over the discipline's active, played games every time a game touching that team is saved, so score edits, flag flips, team swaps and soft deletes all go through the same path and a stale value cannot survive the next save. No migration is needed because the recompute already matches the existing 2024/2026 production data exactly.
nodes.norm_label: league points recomputed from played games, not deltas

nodes.label: Ten new Discipline subclasses for earlier editions

Ten Discipline subclasses (Volleyball, JumpingRope, Dance, Frisbee, Geoguessr, Football, Handball, BurgerQuizz, BlindfoldedObstacleCourse, DiscThrow) are added so those editions can be entered by hand or via import_edition with the right name, result type, icon and French name. Volleyball, Football and Handball are team sports with computed game points like Basketball; the rest have no games and are scored by hand. Frisbee is played golf-style (fewest throws wins) but is scored as ordinary points since there is no 'lowest wins' support yet.

nodes.label: Edition Rank Definition
nodes.rationale: Missing data must never count as a win: a computed (not hand-ranked) edition in which no result has a rank gives every participation a null rank instead of ranking every team 1st on nothing. Decided 2026-09-23 after code review; the 2024 data on prod, still with result_type='NON', is a live case.

nodes.label: Leaderboard Medal-Table Ordering
nodes.rationale: Ranked people are ordered like a medal table on their places (more 1st places first, then more 2nd places, and so on; an extra lower place counts in a person's favour), not by average rank. Revised twice on 2026-09-23: first from an average-based order to this medal-table order, then the teams-beaten share was dropped from the leaderboard's sort entirely (kept only as a displayed figure alongside the average rank).

nodes.label: Manual Ranking via Team.final_rank
nodes.rationale: Lets organisers record a finishing order by hand for an edition without result data. As soon as any active team of an edition carries a final_rank, the whole edition's team ranking switches to that stored order and every team's total_points becomes null, because a computed total would be meaningless without underlying result data; discipline-level standings are left untouched.

nodes.label: Standings Computed in One Pass
nodes.rationale: compute_standings(edition) replaces per-property recomputation (hundreds of queries, e.g. 398 queries / 430ms for one 2024 edition) with three queries computing every discipline rank and team total together; model properties keep their old names but delegate to it, so any caller needing many rows must batch through compute_standings once rather than call the properties in a loop, and the summary serializer is rewritten to pass the standings through context instead of recomputing per row.

nodes.label: Four-Button Theme Switch Mechanism
nodes.rationale: Only the browser knows which theme is on screen and which theme the device prefers, so the header renders all four sun/moon x store/system button combinations and CSS shows exactly one via --switch-to-light/--switch-to-dark; the direction shown always leads away from the theme on screen, and the copy that leads to the device's own theme posts 'system', so toggling twice always returns to the device and the theme cookie only ever records a departure from it.

nodes.label: Hub Stays Dark Regardless of Theme
nodes.rationale: The hub's eclipse is a photograph on black, so a light theme there would look wrong. EditionHub carries data-always-dark; both light CSS blocks exclude themselves with :not(:has([data-always-dark])), so a client-side navigation in or out of the hub flips the theme with no script, and Header hides the whole theme switch form there since it would change nothing visible.
nodes.norm_label: hub stays dark regardless of theme

nodes.label: Duplicated Light Theme Block
nodes.rationale: CSS cannot share one token block between a plain attribute selector and a prefers-color-scheme media query without light-dark(), which would break every token in browsers from before 2024, so the light palette is written twice (data-theme='light', and data-theme='system' nested in the media query) and styles.test.js asserts the two copies stay identical.

nodes.label: Discipline Icon Pictogram Choices
nodes.rationale: Seven discipline models (Relay, Basketball, Petanque, Fair, Obstacle Course, Geography Quizz, General Culture Quizz) had no icon and fell back to the generic star; each pictogram was chosen for silhouette clarity at 70px, e.g. Relay is drawn as a running figure rather than a baton to avoid an ambiguous read at that size.

nodes.label: Badge Rarity (badge_stats)
nodes.rationale: The detail sheet shows what share of players hold a badge, or a tier of it, so a rare badge reads as rare. Computed server-side once per (code, tier) from active rows of active editions in one aggregate query (badge_stats), rather than exposing per-player identity, so a viewer sees '26% of players have it (12 of 47)' without a list of who.

nodes.label: Loopback-Only App Ports for Login Throttle Integrity
nodes.rationale: server, front and their stage counterparts publish only on 127.0.0.1 because the login throttle trusts the last X-Forwarded-For entry (NUM_PROXIES=1); a client reaching Django or the front directly, bypassing nginx, could forge any IP and evade or poison the shared throttle bucket. nginx must therefore be the sole public entry point and must itself set X-Forwarded-For via $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for on every location proxying to server or front.
nodes.norm_label: loopback-only app ports for login throttle integrity

nodes.label: Duplicate Participation Row Resolution
nodes.rationale: When a user has several active Player rows in one edition (it happens today: user 34 has two active 2024 rows), the lowest id among rows with a valid team wins, otherwise the lowest id overall. No database constraint or migration was added: the admin's Player.clean() only blocks new duplicates going forward, while sorting out the existing ones stays a manual admin task.

nodes.label: Self-Hosted Bebas Neue + Inter Fonts
nodes.rationale: Bebas Neue and Inter woff2 files are downloaded once and served from front/static/fonts with font-display: swap and preloaded in app.html, instead of being loaded from Google Fonts at runtime, so the site makes no third-party font request.
